articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Odds and Rankings after Week 9
articles.summary: The favorite for the 2026 Heisman Trophy has shifted.
articles.body:
The favorite for the 2026 Heisman Trophy has shifted.

Although he remains a high-end contender, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is no longer the front-runner. The unfortunate injury to quarterback Julian Sayin cracked the race open, and the Buckeyes fell at USC in their first matchup without the second-year starter.

Subsequently, Smith has slipped behind Miami quarterback Darian Mensah, with Mensah's teammate Malachi Toney hot on Smith's heels.

The final month of the regular season may provide more twists and turns, but the Heisman discussion has a distinct Miami flavor right now.

While the latest FanDuel odds are listed, the rankings are more subjective as a snapshot of this moment in the season.

Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss (+1200)

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State (+5000)

Nate Sheppard, RB, Duke : Welcome back to the fringe of the discussion—and in a monstrous way. Sheppard rushed for 97 yards and racked up five touchdowns in Saturday's rout of Boston College. He's second in the FBS with 1,274 scrimmage yards and stands atop the country with 18 total touchdowns. Duke is 6-2 with a trip to Miami looming after playing at North Carolina State.

Kenny Minchey, QB, Kentucky : Idle last weekend, Minchey and the Cats are ready for their gauntlet. Well, they'd better be, at least. Kentucky has a jaunt to Tennessee in Week 10 before hosting Florida and going to Missouri.

Sam Leavitt, QB, LSU : Similar story for Leavitt, who's set to lead LSU into Saturday's home showdown with rival Alabama. Texas then comes to Baton Rouge, followed by LSU playing at Tennessee. Pretty big three weeks here!

Aidan Chiles, QB, Northwestern : Even though Northwestern lost at Oregon, Chiles deserves a mention. He's thrown for 1,898 yards and 13 touchdowns to one interception, adding 274 yards and 10 scores on the ground.

Michael Hawkins Jr., QB, West Virginia : Hawkins has produced 2,434 offensive yards and 27 touchdowns. Until the Mountaineers lose a fourth game—a potentially fatal blow to his Heisman hopes—he deserves consideration. West Virginia's nightmarish November slate begins with a trip to Texas Tech.

Gunner Stockton, QB, Georgia : Right on the edge of dropping a tier, Stockton mustered 146 yards in UGA's defense-driven win over Florida. This weekend's clash at Ole Miss should be very influential in his award perception.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State : As with Hawkins at WVU, Mestemaker is dealing with a team record issue. Oklahoma State dropped to 5-3 after the dramatic 51-49 loss at Iowa State—a game in which Mestemaker threw for 323 yards and five touchdowns. Still, he's passed for 2,649 yards and 25 scores this year.

CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame : Saturday brings a now-or-never matchup for Carr and Notre Dame. Holding a 7-1 record, the Fighting Irish are poised to host top-ranked Miami—which has a vulnerable, injury-riddled defense. Carr needs a big game for his Heisman résumé, and ND itself needs a marquee win.

Devon Dampier, QB, Utah : Dampier found a bounce-back performance in a comfortable win at Cincinnati, totaling 305 yards and three touchdowns. Utah remains unbeaten, but that perfection will be tested opposite rival BYU this weekend.

Gio Lopez, QB, Wake Forest : Lopez capped a dynamic month with 293 offensive yards and a touchdown in Wake Forest's 51-7 dismantling of Virginia. While propelling the Demon Deacons to a 7-1 record, Lopez has generated 2,493 yards and 24 scores to a lone interception. He should further pad those box-score numbers as Wake Forest hosts FCS team Merrimack in Week 10.

No matter what happens in the rest of Oregon State's campaign, Jesse Legree has made himself a national name as a freshman. Truly, a stellar accomplishment.

Last weekend, though, the Beavers lost to Fresno State and dropped to 5-3. Again, a fourth setback typically is crushing for a Heisman candidate. Voters just do not often recognize star players on average-or-lower teams.

Nevertheless, he remains the FBS leader in both receiving yards (1,110) and touchdowns (14). Legree is atop the Pac-12 with 53 catches, as well.

Against a shaky Texas State defense in Week 10, Legree may shred another secondary. He's not finished in this race.

After a rough, turnover-plagued night in a loss at Texas, Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss recovered to stomp Auburn. He accounted for 328 yards and three touchdowns during the 45-15 blowout.

That's nice. Oh, look, another key game on the horizon.

Second-ranked Georgia is coming to Oxford this weekend, bringing along a defense that forced four turnovers and limited Florida to 246 yards.

Chambliss completed 19 of 36 passes for 263 yards, rushed for 42 yards and accounted for three touchdowns in a 43-35 loss to Georgia during the 2025 regular season.

Miami played with fire twice in October, holding off Florida State in overtime and needing a late score to survive North Carolina.

Most recently, he reeled in seven passes for 75 yards and two scores in a 38-35 escape at UNC. Miami trailed in the fourth quarter, but Toney sparked the comeback with a key explosive play and later sealed the victory with a touchdown.

Depending on Notre Dame's defensive plan, Toney may be headed for a showdown with ND corner Leonard Moore. That'd be a fantastic matchup to watch.

Either way, it'll probably be a tight game in South Bend. And when the 'Canes need a play, everyone in the building will know Toney is their target.

But, unlike FSU or UNC, can Notre Dame stop him?

At this moment, it feels like the Heisman is slipping out of Jeremiah Smith's grasp. We, collectively, spent two weeks talking about the impact of Julian Sayin's presumed absence, and the Buckeyes immediately lost without him.

Smith also snagged 10 receptions for 83 yards and a touchdown in that 30-18 setback at USC. It's not like he was suddenly a non-factor.

If the Buckeyes lose again and exit the College Football Playoff race, it's hard to imagine Smith's award upside won't tumble, too. If they rattle off a winning streak, however, it's similarly likely that Smith was the catalyst.

OSU's final stretch, starting at home against Oregon, is a narrative-setter for Smith.

Miami, you have a defensive problem. Injuries have wrecked the secondary, and the 'Canes have allowed at least 400 yards and at least six yards per play in three consecutive games—despite winning all three.

Good thing Darian Mensah is a problem for all defenses, huh?

Miami only had seven possessions at North Carolina, yet the quarterback oversaw six scoring drives. He completed 22-of-29 attempts for 274 yards and three touchdowns, adding 36 yards on the ground and answering every UNC threat that arose.

Notre Dame boasts a stellar, even if also banged-up, defense that is certain to test Mensah. All these good, positive statements may be quieter in a week's time.

On the other hand, Mensah may leave South Bend with his signature moment.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Top 20 College Football QBs after Week 9
articles.summary: Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.
articles.body:
Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.

Included are each player's numbers through the air and on the ground, their game's outcome, and the quality of their opponent. A 1-5 star system was used to highlight the quality of the opponent, using the most recent version of The Athletic's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, with stars awarded as follows:

5 stars: No. 1-10 in the rankings 4 stars: No. 11-40 in the rankings 3 stars: No. 41-70 in the rankings 2 stars: No. 71-100 in the rankings 1 star: No. 101-138 in the rankings or an FCS opponent

Each quarterback's performance was given a grade of A, B, C, D or F. Those grades were factored into the reordering of the rankings for the following week.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 24-of-33, 236 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, -2 yards, 2 TD Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Texas State) Week 9 Outcome: Win (46-45)

With less than eight minutes remaining and Boise State trailing 39-28 following an interception return touchdown by Texas State on the Broncos' previous possession, Maddux Madsen was knocked out of the game with a left knee injury.

Max Cutforth replaced him and promptly led three straight drives that all ended in passing touchdowns, as he finished 8-of-13 for 131 yards and three scores to help Boise State avoid the upset.

Madsen eventually returned to the sidelines on crutches, and his status going forward is unclear.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 16-of-30, 263 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, -2 yards, 1 TD Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Utah) Week 9 Outcome: Loss (25-49)

After throwing a career-high four touchdown passes in an upset victory over Texas Tech in Week 8, JC French IV had a significantly less impactful game against Utah on Saturday.

It was his second game this season without a touchdown pass, and his 53.3 percent completion rate was the worst single-game showing of the year. The schedule doesn't get any easier next week when the Bearcats hit the road to face No. 17 Houston.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 20-of-31, 179 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 3 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Arkansas) Week 9 Outcome: Win (34-10)

With 211 rushing yards as a team, including another big game from Jamal Roberts (23 carries, 138 yards, 1 TD), Missouri didn't need Austin Simmons to shoulder the offensive load in Saturday's lopsided victory over Arkansas.

It wasn't the most efficient passing game for the Ole Miss transfer, but he still added two more touchdowns to his season total, and his 16-to-2 touchdown-to-interception ratio on the year remains excellent. Now the grind begins for the Tigers, as they face Texas, Georgia and Kentucky the next three weeks.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 19-of-24, 301 yards, 3 TD, 2 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 13 carries, 96 yards, 2 TD Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Oklahoma) Week 9 Outcome: Win (42-25)

After an 0-3 start to SEC play, South Carolina has won three in a row against Florida, Tennessee and Oklahoma, and that is enough to make them the highest-ranked three-loss team in the latest AP poll at No. 23.

During that three-game winning streak, LaNorris Sellers has piled up 790 passing yards, 212 rushing yards and 13 total touchdowns. There is still room to clean up his decision making, with his two interceptions on Saturday bringing his season total to seven, but his dynamic dual-threat playmaking has been the catalyst for their rise to relevance.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 33-of-46, 404 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, 41 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Florida Atlantic) Week 9 Outcome: Win (48-41)

In a matchup of two of the best Group of Six quarterbacks in the nation, Tayven Jackson and North Texas outpaced Caden Veltkamp (37/56, 452 yards, 5 TD, 1 INT) and Florida Atlantic to improve to 6-2 overall and stay undefeated in AAC play.

After stops at Tennessee, Indiana and UCF, Jackson is finally realizing the potential that made him a 4-star recruit out of high school. He leads the AAC in completion percentage (72.3) and passing yards (2,577), and his passer rating (176.8) is good for fifth among all FBS quarterbacks.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 29-of-35, 371 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 30 yards, 1 TD Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Army) Week 9 Outcome: Win (49-22)

Memphis is 5-1 in its last six games, and while Marcus Stokes had a three-interception dud in the lone loss to Tulane, he has 18 touchdown passes and zero interceptions in the five victories during that stretch.

He leads the AAC in passer rating (178.5) and yards per attempt (9.8), and he is tied for the FBS lead in passing touchdowns (25) and total touchdowns (28) in his first season at the FBS level.

A tough game on the road against South Florida is up next, as the Bulls' defense is surrendering just 14.5 points per game.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 8-of-19, 119 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 2 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Minnesota) Week 9 Outcome: Win (23-16)

After a shaky first half where he also took a big hit just before halftime, Josh Hoover was benched in favor of Grant Wilson, who ultimately threw the game-winning touchdown pass on the first play of overtime.

With 12 of his 19 touchdown passes this season coming against North Texas, Howard and Rutgers, Hoover's overall numbers look better than the recent results. In his last four games, he has completed just 48.5 percent of his passes with four touchdowns and two interceptions. With a bye this weekend, the Hoosiers have two weeks to sort out who is going to start against USC on Nov. 14.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 22-of-29, 260 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, 45 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Cincinnati) Week 9 Outcome: Win (49-25)

The Utes scored on all four of their offensive possessions during the first half of Saturday's game, and the defense also added a pair of scores to build a 42-6 halftime lead.

That meant the running game took center stage after the break, but Devon Dampier still put together a strong overall game, and he capped off the scoring with his third touchdown pass of the day late in the third quarter. A solid bounce-back performance after his shaky showing against Houston in Week 8.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 20-of-28, 250 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, 62 yards, 1 TD Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Stanford) Week 9 Outcome: Win (52-24)

For the fourth time this season, Lincoln Kienholz had at least two passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown. He is now up to 23 total touchdowns on the year, with 12 passing and 11 rushing, and the Louisville offense ranks fifth in the nation with 40.5 points per game.

After a disappointing 2-3 start to the year, the Cardinals have outscored the opposition 130-70 during a three-game winning streak against Florida State, Syracuse and Stanford. With one year of eligibility left, Kienholz is laying the groundwork for what could be a legitimate star turn in 2027.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 22-of-38, 281 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT

Week 9 Rushing Stats: 14 carries, 93 yards, 1 TD

Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Oregon)

After building a 20–6 lead with two touchdowns and two field goals on their first four possessions, Northwestern's offense stalled in the second half. The Wildcats punted three times and attempted three field goals, making two, en route to their second loss of the year.

With 13 passing touchdowns and 10 rushing touchdowns on the year after his two first-half scores on Saturday, Aidan Chiles is now one of only four FBS quarterbacks with double digits in both categories. Lincoln Kienholz (Louisville), Michael Hawkins Jr. (West Virginia) and Ashton Daniels (Florida State) are the others.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 19-of-29, 210 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 2 carries, 4 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Navy) Week 9 Outcome: Win (35-13)

The Fighting Irish led just 14-13 at halftime against Navy, but they responded with three straight touchdown drives spanning 219 total yards to take control of the game in the second half.

While all three of those scoring drives were punctuated by rushing touchdowns, CJ Carr did have a pair of touchdown passes, bouncing back from a lackluster performance in the Week 7 loss to BYU. Eight games into the season, Carr has a remarkably similar completion percentage (66.6 to 66.7) and passer rating (168.1 to 162.5) to a year ago.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 22-of-34, 263 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 65 yards, 1 TD Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Auburn) Week 9 Outcome: Win (45-15)

The Rebels led 17-15 midway through the third quarter before rattling off 28 unanswered points to close out the game, and that decisive stretch included all three of Trinidad Chambliss' touchdowns.

The SEC leader in completions (189), passing yards (2,189) and passing touchdowns (18), he also threw his eighth interception of the season on Saturday. He has a chance at a career-defining game this Saturday against No. 2 Georgia, with a victory likely putting Ole Miss comfortably in the playoff picture.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 15-of-22, 222 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 1 carry, -9 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★★ (Ohio State) Week 9 Outcome: Win (30-18)

Jayden Maiava became the first quarterback this season to complete more than 65 percent of his passes against the Ohio State defense, and that efficiency helped the Trojans pull off the upset victory.

He has now reached 20 touchdown passes for the second straight season, and leads the Big Ten in that category, as well as completions (198) and passing yards (2,524).

One week after falling out of the AP Top 25 entirely after a loss to Wisconsin, the Trojans are back to No. 18 with an extra week to plan for their Nov. 14 matchup with Indiana.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 27-of-42, 323 yards, 5 TD, 1 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, 16 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Iowa State) Week 9 Outcome: Loss (49-51)

Most weeks, 49 points is going to win a college football game, but that wasn't enough on Saturday as Oklahoma State took a 51-49 loss to Iowa State for its second Big 12 loss and third loss overall.

With his seventh 300-yard passing performance in eight games, Drew Mestemaker did his part, also tossing five touchdown passes for the second time this season. Now tied for the FBS lead with 25 touchdown passes, Mestemaker is making a solid case to be QB1 on the 2027 NFL draft board, but there's a lot of season left.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 33-of-45, 417 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 10 carries, -25 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Texas Tech) Week 9 Outcome: Loss (26-34)

Arizona led 23-17 midway through the third quarter in Saturday's high-profile showdown with Texas Tech, but the Wildcats offense went punt, turnover on downs, punt, punt and field goal over their final five possessions to give the Red Raiders a path to victory.

With just 12 rushing yards on 30 carries, the Arizona offense landed almost exclusively on Noah Fifita's shoulders. With 33 completions and 417 passing yards, he did everything he could, but Texas Tech's defense did just enough down the stretch to secure the win.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 29-of-36, 351 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 13 carries, -5 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Syracuse) Week 9 Outcome: Loss (27-30)

Kevin Jennings had a strong individual performance on Saturday, but the end result was a crushing loss to a Syracuse team that entered the game 3-4 overall and 1-4 in ACC play.

Syracuse snatched the victory with 10 unanswered points to close out the game, sandwiched around a three-and-out for the SMU offense where Jennings took a six-yard loss on a sack on second down. He was sacked six times total, and SMU averaged just 2.2 yards per carry.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 13-of-23, 101 yards, 0 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 12 carries, 45 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Florida) Week 9 Outcome: Win (27-8)

With 42 rushing attempts for 217 yards and two touchdowns, the Georgia offense leaned heavily on the running game in Saturday's victory, largely taking things out of Gunner Stockton's hands.

He did tie for the team lead with 12 carries for 45 yards, but his season-low 101 passing yards came on the heels of a two-interception game in their Week 7 loss to Auburn.

It's fair to wonder if Stockton will be relegated to more of a game-manager role going forward, or if this was just a Florida-specific game plan.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 13-of-21, 229 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 13 carries, 64 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Virginia) Week 9 Outcome: Win (51-7)

In five games since losing to Miami in their ACC opener, Wake Forest has outscored the opposition 217-58, and they don't face another ranked opponent the rest of the way. They currently sit at No. 14 in the AP poll, but this team has a legitimate path to the College Football Playoff field.

A big part of their success has been the play of Gio Lopez, who has completed 67.1 percent of his passes for 2,176 yards and 18 touchdowns against only one interception. He also has 317 rushing yards and six rushing scores, and he should have a chance to pad his stats against FCS opponent Merrimack on Saturday.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 33-of-59, 373 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 9 carries, -14 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Fresno State) Week 9 Outcome: Loss (22-38)

While those 373 passing yards jump off the page, the high-powered Oregon State offense sputtered with three turnovers on downs, two lost fumbles and two punts, and Braden Atkinson was responsible for both fumbles.

He still leads the nation with 2,977 passing yards, while his 25 touchdown passes are tied atop the FBS leaderboard, but the Beavers' third loss is a critical blow to their hopes of chasing down Boise State for the Group of Six playoff spot.

Week 9 Passing Stats: 22-of-29, 274 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 9 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, 36 yards Week 9 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (North Carolina) Week 9 Outcome: Win (38-35)

The Miami defense was the reason Saturday's game against North Carolina was closer than expected, as the Hurricanes surrendered 407 total yards and 35 points, both season-high marks in a regulation game.

On offense, Darian Mensah was his usual efficient self under center, while Malachi Toney (7 catches, 75 yards, 2 TD) still did damage even in a game where he was somewhat contained. Mensah remains the Heisman Trophy front-runner, and Miami avoided taking a loss in its worst defensive performance of the season.

To keep things fresh and include breakout performers, we will re-rank the top 20 quarterbacks each week. That will then reset the field for next week's report cards.

Quarterbacks with a Week 10 bye who are performing at a top-20 level were still included in the updated rankings to show how they stack up to the field.

However, since there will be no Week 10 performance to grade, they are presented with "***" rather than a ranking number and will not appear in next week's article.

articles.title: Uriarte: "En el Athletic tiene repercusión hasta el cambio de patrocinio en las botellas de agua"
articles.standfirst: Los presidentes de Athletic y Real coinciden en una charla auspiaciada por Elkargi
articles.summary: Los presidentes de Athletic y Real coinciden en una charla auspiaciada por Elkargi
articles.body: El derbi del domingo en San Mamés ha tenido continuidad este martes en la Torre BAT de Bilbao, donde Jon Uriarte y Jokin Aperribay han debatido del ámbito empresarial en un acto organizado por la institución financiera Elkargi. Lejos de las polémicas del terreno de juego los dos presidentes han dado impresiones acerca del fútbol y la empresa. El dirigente del Athletic ha destacado que “siento que el club está permanentemente evaluado y yo también me siento así. Cualquier decisión que tomas es una decisión que sabes van a evaluar y muchas veces se hace de manera irrespetuosa. En el Athletic tiene una repercusión brutal hasta cambiar el patrocinio de las botellas de agua”, explicó. El presidente Uriarte señaló que “la gobernanza es parecida en un club y en una empresa porque estamos en un entorno competitivo muy salvaje. Pero hay elementos diferentes: el fútbol es una industria muy emocional. Apple y Amazon tienen sus seguidores, pero nadie deja a su equipo de fútbol. El componente emocional hace que todo lo que rodea al club tenga una repercusión brutal”, dijo. El reelegido presidente por otras cuatro temporadas sin necesidad de pasar por las urnas porque no tuvo ningún candidato en contra apuntó que “aunque pretendas una gestión a largo plazo, el examen es cada partido, semanal. Otra diferencia es que en el fútbol muestras el nivel que tienen tus trabajadores, los jugadores, y te los pueden fichar otros, algo que no pasa en las empresas. Estás muy expuesto”.

articles.title: Scott Parker: Rob Green and John Moncur back West Ham move
articles.summary: Rob Green says Scott Parker's "proven record" of getting teams promoted makes him a perfect fit as the club's next boss.
articles.body:
Former West Ham United goalkeeper Rob Green says Scott Parker's "proven record" of getting teams promoted from the Championship would make him the perfect fit as the club's next manager.

Parker, 46, is expected to replace Nuno Espirito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday following West Ham's disappointing start to the season after relegation.

A three-time former club player of the year at West Ham, Parker has led Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion as a manager.

"Scott's shown a proven record of getting promoted," Green, a former team-mate of Parker's, told BBC Radio London.

"Detractors of Scott would say, 'this is not a really imaginative style of play, it's not one that might thrill the fans'. I think Scott would say, 'well, actually, my team knows exactly what it needs to do to get promoted'.

"There's so much quality in that side that they should still get promoted. You get in the Premier League, you stay in the Premier League, then you worry about the style of football.

"Give the stardust in that [West Ham] front line to him [and] he can give you a really good platform to go forwards with it. It makes perfect sense to me."

Widely seen as favourites for automatic promotion after dropping out of the Premier League last season, West Ham are currently eighth in the Championship, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough.

They have won two of their last six games and have lost back-to-back home matches - going down 3-2 to Southampton and then 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.

The decision to sack Nuno means West Ham are looking for their fourth permanent manager since David Moyes left the London Stadium in May 2024.

Another former West Ham player, John Moncur, said the club were too hasty in letting Moyes go, but also backed Parker for the job.

"I don't think we would have been in this position if Moyes had stayed, because he's that type of manager that wouldn't have allowed the things to happen that did," Moncur told BBC Radio London.

"[Scott] has done a good job at other clubs, he knows the club backwards and it seems to fit.

"They are a very educated bunch of fans, you can't pull the wool over their eyes. Scott will know that.

"It's getting the balance right. It's no good playing lovely football if you're not winning matches."

articles.title: El Valencia maneja más de 52.000 abonados para el traslado al Nou Mestalla
articles.standfirst: Más de 47.600 aficionados se han agrupado para elegir asiento junto a familiares, amigos o peñistas en el nuevo estadio a falta de tres días del cierre de plazo
articles.summary: Más de 47.600 aficionados se han agrupado para elegir asiento junto a familiares, amigos o peñistas en el nuevo estadio a falta de tres días del cierre de plazo
articles.body: A falta de tres días para que concluya la creación de agrupaciones del Nou Mestalla, el Valencia ya dispone de una fotografía bastante precisa de la demanda que tendrá el futuro estadio. Los datos del club reflejan la existencia de 52.329 abonados potenciales, una cifra que equivale a cerca de tres cuartas partes de los más de 70.000 asientos con los que contará el recinto. Hasta el momento se han creado 13.028 grupos, de las cuales 12.939 ya están completamente confirmados, según ha contado Radio MARCA Valencia. Además, aparecen 1.311 agrupaciones individuales, es decir, se han confirmado con una sola persona. El tamaño medio de estos conjuntos alcanza los 3,65 integrantes, una cifra que refleja la tendencia de muchos aficionados a organizarse para mantener la proximidad con familiares, amigos o compañeros de peña en el nuevo recinto. Pese al elevado grado de participación, el proceso todavía deja margen para los rezagados. Según los datos del club, todavía hay 4.722 abonados que no forman parte de ningún grupo y 3.708 Socios VCF pendientes de completar el trámite. De estos últimos, 1.820 corresponden a nuevas altas realizadas esta temporada. La diferencia entre ambos colectivos es relevante desde el punto de vista operativo. Los abonados que no hayan realizado ninguna gestión seguirán estando incluidos en el proceso de asignación de asientos, ya que el sistema los considerará de forma automática como una agrupación individual. Sin embargo, los Socios VCF no abonados sí deben registrarse expresamente en la plataforma, aunque sea para crear un grupo de una sola persona. De no hacerlo, no recibirán la correspondiente cita para las siguientes fases del traslado al Nou Mestalla. El Valencia abrió inicialmente la fase de creación de grupos el pasado 14 de octubre y, ante la respuesta de los aficionados, amplió el plazo hasta el próximo 6 de noviembre a las 12.00 horas. Se trata de un trámite exclusivamente online y considerado clave dentro del proceso, ya que es el único momento en el que los aficionados pueden decidir con quién desean sentarse en el futuro estadio. Una vez finalice esta fase, el club procesará todas las solicitudes y determinará el orden de citación para la elección presencial de localidades contiguas. Para ello, cada agrupación cuenta con la figura de un capitán, encargado de representar al grupo durante los siguientes pasos del traslado. El proceso entra así en su recta final con la mayoría de la masa social ya organizada.

articles.title: Tenerife's Jesus de Miguel Dies At Age 30 After On-Field Collision
articles.summary: Tenerife announced Tuesday that forward Jesús de Miguel died at the age of 30 due to injuries he suffered in Monday's 2-2 draw with FC Andorra.
articles.body:
Tenerife announced Tuesday that forward Jesús de Miguel died at the age of 30 due to injuries he suffered in Monday's 2-2 draw with FC Andorra.

"Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," the club said (via BBC Sport ).

"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can lessen this overwhelming sadness. We stand with his grieving family, with his loved ones, with all of Tenerife who mourn this cruel loss today."

De Miguel came on as a substitute in the 59th minute of the match. With Tenerife attempting to score a late winner, he collided with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono while tracking a long pass.

Trainers immediately tended to De Miguel on the pitch, and he was transported away by an ambulance to be treated for chest and head injuries. The referee brought the match to a halt given the severity of the situation.

Tenerife initially described De Miguel's status as "stable" but said Tuesday his "medical condition has deteriorated neurologically."

De Miguel was in his second season with Tenerife, having signed with the club from Castellón in July 2025. He had scored 11 goals in 36 appearances.

The Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) announced it's suspending all matches Tuesday, while UEFA said it will hold a moment of silence before its fixtures this week.

"We are heartbroken by the death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda," UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin said in a statement. "We have searched for words and found only silence. In that silence, our hearts and thoughts are with his family, his teammates, everyone at CD Tenerife, and all those who mourn this tragic loss."

European clubs such as Arsenal and Real Madrid have also paid tribute to De Miguel with a moment of silence during their training sessions on Tuesday.

articles.summary: Scotland will meet Germany, Netherlands and Sweden in the next edition of the women's Nations League.
articles.body:
Scotland will meet Germany, Netherlands and Sweden in the next edition of the women's Nations League.

Melissa Andreatta's side are preparing for a World Cup play-off with the Swedes in December.

Scotland, who were in the lowest tier of seeds in the A division, met Germany and the Dutch in the 2025 competition.

They lost 6-1 and 4-0 to Germany, but the games against Netherlands were much closer, with a 2-1 home defeat and a 1-1 draw in Tilburg.

Scotland lost 4-0 and 1-0 to the Dutch in 2023.

Sweden and Scotland last met in a 2021 friendly in Paisley, with the visitors prevailing 2-0.

On the impending showdown with Sweden, Andreatta said: "I'm glad we can narrow in on what's ahead of us immediately and that's performing in these next two games.

"The last two games against the Czech Republic was exactly the kind of preparation we needed."

Captain Caroline Weir has not played for Lyon since pulling up in the warm-up before the second leg at home to the Czechs but Andreatta said the star midfielder "is progressing well and to plan".

articles.title: Saudi Pro League postpones matches after Asian Cup rescheduling
articles.summary: League delays matches after revised Asian Cup dates create ‘additional flexibility in the domestic football calendar’.
articles.body:
Matches in Saudi Arabia’s premier football league scheduled for the coming week have been postponed after the rescheduling of the AFC Asian Cup 2027, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) says.

“The decision comes as part of a wider review of the ⁠⁠2026-27 league ⁠⁠fixture schedule, with the revised Asian Cup dates creating additional flexibility in the domestic football calendar,” the SPL said ⁠⁠in a statement on Tuesday, two days before the start of the match week.

The postponement of the Asian Cup until December next year was announced earlier in the day after recent attacks on the kingdom. The 24-team continental tournament had been due to take place from January 7 to February 5.

Asian football’s governing body announced the decision after “extensive discussions and close consultation with the Local Organising Committee (LOC) of the AFC Asian Cup Saudi Arabia 2027 and the Saudi Arabian Football Federation (SAFF)”.

The tournament will now run from December 23, 2027, to January 21, 2028.

An attack on Riyadh’s international airport last month killed at least 13 ‌‌people and wounded more than 300. Yemen’s Houthis claimed responsibility for the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade. Further attacks on the airport in the span of a week killed at least five more people.

“New ⁠⁠dates for matchweek 13 ⁠⁠will be announced once the review is complete.”

The SPL has rescheduled several domestic league games this season for logistical ‌‌reasons, and last month’s AFC Champions League Elite clash in Riyadh between hosts Al-Nassr and Emirati ‌‌side ‌‌Al Wasl was postponed due to a threat of missile attacks.

Kickoff was delayed after Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defence issued a safety warning 15 minutes before ⁠⁠the scheduled start time.

articles.title: Spanish footballer Jesús de Miguel’s death: What next for goalkeeper Jesús Owono? Sporting sanctions and possible criminal proceedings
articles.summary: The death of Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel following an on-field collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono has plunged Spanish football into
articles.body: The death of Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel following an on-field collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono has plunged Spanish football into mourning. But as tributes pour in for the 30-year-old forward, attention has also turned to what could happen next for the goalkeeper involved in the tragic incident, including the possibility of sporting sanctions and criminal proceedings.Owono, an Equatorial Guinea international, is reportedly in a state of shock following the incident and is deeply affected by De Miguel's death. The goalkeeper has also faced a wave of abuse on social media, with some users directing personal insults at him and calling him a "murderer".However, the tragic outcome does not, by itself, establish that Owono committed an offence. Any sporting or legal consequences will depend on an assessment of the challenge, the circumstances surrounding it and the applicable rules. The two processes are separate and must not be confused with the grief surrounding De Miguel's death.What happened in the collision?The incident took place during Tenerife's Spanish second-division match against Andorra on Monday. De Miguel appeared to be chasing a long ball near the halfway line as Tenerife looked for a late winner. Owono rushed out of his area to clear the ball but collided with the forward, striking him in the chest with his knee.De Miguel went down and received medical attention on the pitch for more than five minutes. He was eventually taken away by ambulance, while Owono was shown a red card. The match was abandoned in the seventh minute of stoppage time with the score at 2-2.Spanish media reported that De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived in the ambulance. His condition deteriorated overnight, and Tenerife confirmed his death on Tuesday.The club paid an emotional tribute, saying: "Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda."What sporting sanction could Owono face?From a disciplinary perspective, the Spanish Football Federation's Disciplinary Code provides for sanctions for violent conduct during a match.Article 102 stipulates a suspension of between four to 12 matches for players who engage in violent conduct against an opponent during play and cause serious injury or harm. The provision could be considered when assessing Owono's challenge, but its application is not automatic.The disciplinary authorities would have to examine the nature of the challenge, the goalkeeper's actions and the circumstances in which the collision occurred before deciding whether the article applies and what sanction, if any, is appropriate.The fact that De Miguel subsequently died does not automatically mean that Owono will receive the maximum 12-match suspension. The final decision would rest with the relevant disciplinary body after examining the available evidence.Could the goalkeeper face criminal proceedings?The more serious question is whether the incident could lead to criminal proceedings. Under Spanish law, a death during a sporting contest does not automatically rule out criminal liability. However, neither does a fatal outcome automatically establish a crime.Article 142 of the Spanish Penal Code deals with negligent homicide, distinguishing between gross negligence and less serious negligence.In cases involving gross negligence, the prescribed punishment is imprisonment for one to four years. Where the negligence is classified as less serious, the law provides for a fine of three to 18 months.These are the general penalties under the law, not an indication that Owono will necessarily be charged or convicted.For criminal liability to be established, investigators and, ultimately, the courts would need to examine whether the goalkeeper's conduct amounted to criminally relevant negligence. That would involve assessing whether he breached the duty of care expected in the circumstances, whether the fatal outcome was reasonably foreseeable and avoidable, and whether the required causal link between his actions and De Miguel's death can be established.The distinction between an unfortunate sporting collision and criminal negligence is crucial. A challenge that results in a tragic injury or death is not, on that basis alone, proof of a criminal act.Two separate processes, one deeply painful tragedyAny disciplinary action by the football authorities would be independent of a possible criminal investigation. The federation would assess the incident under its sporting regulations, while criminal liability, if investigated, would be a matter for the appropriate legal authorities and courts.The federation's regulations also provide for the possibility of referring incidents to the Public Prosecutor's Office when there are indications of a criminal offence.For now, the focus remains on De Miguel and the people mourning his loss. The striker joined Tenerife in 2025 and scored 11 goals in 30 appearances, helping the club secure promotion from Spain's third division. He had previously played important roles in promotion campaigns with Internacional de Madrid and CD Castellón.FC Andorra expressed its condolences to De Miguel's family, teammates and Tenerife, while the Spanish Footballers Association described his death as a loss that left a huge void in the football community.The questions surrounding Owono's future will be addressed through the relevant sporting and legal processes. But no sanction or legal finding should be presumed before those processes have run their course. At the centre of this tragedy is the death of a footballer following an on-field collision, and the grief of a family and a football community left to come to terms with an unimaginable loss.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel dies after on-pitch collision with opponent, Spanish police open investigation
articles.summary: Jesús de Miguel joined Tenerife on a three-year deal in 2025.
articles.body:
Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died Tuesday following an in-pitch collision during Monday's game, the team announced. He was 30.

In the closing seconds of Tenerife's game against Andorra, de Miguel was involved in a brutal collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono around midfield.

Owono was immediately handed a red card and began walking off the pitch. De Miguel initially laid with his head and knees on the grass before turning onto his back. He then became motionless, resulting in an opposing player immediately calling to the sideline for help. Once Owono realized the severity of the situation, he stopped walking off the field and turned back to check on de Miguel. Owono faces a suspension for the collision.

Additionally, Spanish police have reportedly opened an investigation into the situation looking at a possible involuntary manslaughter charge, per ABC News.

The match did not continue following the incident. The match was tied 2-2 at the time play was suspended. De Miguel was transferred to a hospital and was initially deemed " stable despite the severity of his condition ," Tenerife said in a statement after the game. Later in the day, however, the team said de Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically."

On Tuesday morning, Tenerife announced de Miguel's death. The team's statement, which was translated from Spanish to English, read:

Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic passing, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesús de Miguel Alameda. There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness. We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones, alongside all of tinerfeñismo that today weeps for this cruel outcome. The family of Jesús de Miguel thanks each and every one of the expressions of support received, and likewise requests, from the heart, the utmost respect for their privacy in these terrible moments.

In the wake of the news, Andorra also released a statement sending their " most sincere condolences " to de Miguel's family.

Both Real Madrid and FC Barcelona issued statements expressing their condolences and extending support to de Miguel's family. De Miguel was born in Madrid.

Lionel Messi also paid tribute to de Miguel in a post on Instagram.

Following de Miguel's death, the Royal Spanish Football Federation announced all matches would be suspended Tuesday.

De Miguel began his senior career in 2015 and played for eight different teams. He joined Tenerife on a three-year deal in 2025 and had 11 goals in 34 appearances with the club.

articles.title: Unos 6.000 béticos desafiarán al Muro Amarillo en el Signal Iduna Park
articles.standfirst: Uno de los mayores desplazamientos de la afición del Betis sin tratarse de una final
articles.summary: Uno de los mayores desplazamientos de la afición del Betis sin tratarse de una final
articles.body: El partido entre el Betis y el Borussia Dortmund que se disputa este miércoles en el Signal Iduna Park a partir de las 21.00 horas, correspondiente a la cuarta jornada de la fase de liga de la Champions League, registrará uno de los mayores desplazamientos de la historia verdiblanca sin tratarse de una final. La visita al Signal Iduna Park, uno de los grandes, míticos y más imponentes estadios del fútbol europeo, es la salida que más ilusiona a la afición verdiblanca. El partido en Dortmund es la segunda cita a domicilio del equipo de Manuel Pellegrini en Champions tras la victoria contra el Lille (2-3). Oporto (3-2) y Feyenoord (1-0) también cayeron, en este caso, en sus visitas a La Cartuja. El presidente verdiblanco Ángel Haro tiró de prudencia esta mañana a pesar del pleno de los andaluces y descartó hablar de objetivos a largo plazo como el 'top-8': "Hay que centrarse en el siguiente partido. De nada sirve que estemos hablando del top-8 si ahora pierdes dos o tres partidos". Todavía quedan rivales muy importantes como el Arsenal o el Bayern de Múnich. El equipo no estará solo. El Dortmund sólo ha perdido dos de sus últimos 24 partidos (15 victorias y siete empates) de Champions como local y cuenta con la Südtribüne, el Muro Amarillo. Considerada la mayor tribuna de pie de Europa, reúne a casi 24.500 aficionados. Serán minoría, pero algo más de 6.000 béticos respaldarán a los suyos. Una cifra que se aproximará a la registrada en octubre de 2018 en Milán, cuando cerca de 7.000 seguidores acompañaron al equipo en su enfrentamiento con el Milan en la Europa League. El Borussia Dortmund facilitó 3.813 localidades al Betis, que se agotaron rápidamente. A esta cifra hay que sumar otras 200 entradas destinadas al protocolo del club verdiblanco y alrededor de 2.300 que han sido adquiridas directamente por aficionados béticos a través de los canales de venta del conjunto alemán. El enfrentamiento ante el Borussia Dortmund es inédito para los verdiblancos. Sí pisaron tierras germanas con un balance de una victoria (1-3 en Kaiserslautern en la Copa de la UEFA de la temporada 95-96), dos empates (Recopa de Europa del curso 77-78 frente al Lokomotive Leipzig y en Frankfurt, ante el Eintracht en la temporada 2021-2022) y una derrota (4-0 en la fase de grupos frente al Bayer Leverkusen de la campaña 2021-2022).

Crystal Palace are appealing against Jean-Philippe Mateta's red card in the defeat by Tottenham on Saturday.

The striker was shown a straight red card by referee Michael Oliver for a late challenge on Micky van de Ven when the game was still 0-0, after just 13 minutes.

Oliver originally gave a yellow card but it was upgraded after a VAR review.

Mateta caught the Spurs defender on top of the ankle but in Palace's view the impact was accidental.

It is understood the 29-year-old forward believes his eyes were on the ball and that he did not see Van de Ven.

The France international is facing a three-match suspension but Palace hope the decision is either overturned or his ban reduced.

Palace face Liverpool this weekend in a game that could have a bearing on manager Pierre Sage's long-term future at the club following a disappointing start to his reign.

articles.title: William Saliba's return gives Mikel Arteta selection headache at Arsenal
articles.summary: William Saliba returning to first-team training before Arsenal's game with Slavia Prague in the Champions League is a huge boost for the club but now presents Mikel Arteta with a selection headache.
articles.body:
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta will soon have a big defensive dilemma.

But it is one that will be both welcome to the Arsenal boss and the envy of other top teams across the continent.

That's because William Saliba - a key figure in the Gunners' title win last season - is back in training, having missed the entire campaign so far because of a back injury following his early withdrawal in France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain.

The 25-year-old has been one of the Premier League's top defenders in recent seasons but - in his absence - summer signing Ezri Konsa has stepped in seamlessly to help Arsenal back to the top of the table.

Indeed, since Konsa's arrival from Aston Villa for £55m, he and Gabriel Magalhaes have struck up a formidable partnership, with Arsenal again boasting the league's tightest defence, conceding just five goals in nine games.

Saliba had been managing his back issue throughout last season but was sent to see a specialist after the World Cup.

It was decided he did not need to undergo surgery but would require a lengthy rehabilitation. No timescale on his return was set.

The France international had been doing individual training at Arsenal 's base but has now returned to full training before their Champions League meeting with Slavia Prague and then, a busy festive schedule looming.

Saliba and regular partner Gabriel were a huge reason why the Gunners won the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years last season.

Their partnership was the bedrock of Arteta's team, which conceded only 27 league goals. Saliba was then named in the PFA team of the year for the fourth consecutive time.

Arsenal have always said that they will be cautious with Saliba's return but his return to fitness will leave Arteta with some tough choices to make in his backline.

No Saliba, no problem - Konsa stepping up for Arsenal

How Arteta is getting the best from Rice

Such was Arsenal 's strength in defence, there were questions about whether they needed to sign Konsa when the Gunners decided to spend £55m on the England international.

But the centre-back has been one of the club's best players this season as they sit top of the Premier League.

Some have even suggested Konsa and Gabriel have become the best partnership in world football , external .

Arsenal already had seven senior defenders when they signed Konsa including one of the most solid and well-established partnerships in world football in Saliba and Gabriel.

But in Saliba's absence, Konsa has started seven of Arsenal 's nine Premier League matches, having joined just hours before their opening match against Coventry before coming on against former club Aston Villa for his debut.

And Arteta has said the way that Konsa has settled for the Gunners has been "unbelievable".

The defender made 286 appearances for Villa after joining in July 2019 from Brentford and helped them win the Europa League in May, the club's first European trophy since 1982.

He has established himself as a first-choice starter for England and started seven of the eight games the Three Lions played at the World Cup.

And what could now prove a big clue to his Arsenal future - he started the quarter-final against Norway at right back.

Konsa is an imposing figure, quick across the ground, and his aggression in challenges has impressed supporters.

The 29-year-old scored the opener against Everton in Arsenal 's 2-0 win and put in another commanding performance as the Gunners beat Liverpool at Anfield for the first time in 14 years on Sunday.

Arsenal host Hull on Saturday before the next international break starts this month.

That time will allow Saliba to further build up his fitness before he will become a regular option again for Arteta.

However, when Saliba does return, Arteta is going to have to disappoint someone.

Ben White and Jurrien Timber have been Arsenal 's first choice right-backs this season and are dependable top-level options.

Both have previously had fitness issues but White has been available for all but one of Arsenal 's games this campaign.

Konsa could move to right-back, a position he also made his England debut in, which would allow Saliba to slot in next to Gabriel in his regular spot.

Arteta values physicality in his Arsenal side and moving Konsa, who is physically imposing, to right-back would give opposition attackers a formidable challenge.

Saliba's return also lowers the chance of game time for young centre-back Cristhian Mosquera and his low number of minutes so far this season will raise questions about his future, even though he has recovered from a hamstring injury.

The Gunners played 63 games in all competitions last season as they won the league and reached the Champions League final.

And, with Arteta aiming to defend the title and have European success this time out, there will be a lot of games for him to rotate his many options.

articles.title: College football's playoff picture is a mess. Good luck making sense of it
articles.summary: After a chaotic start to the college football season, very few fan bases will be happy when the inaugural CFP rankings are unveiled on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
If you're reading this prior to Tuesday night, there's a group of men and women who need your thoughts and prayers.

Yes, they may be cloistered in a five-star resort near the Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. Yes, they may be enjoying catered meals including creamed spinach, cowboy corn and an assorted dessert bar. And yes, they may be wasting their own and everyone else's time by even participating in this project.

But the College Football Playoff selection committee, maybe for the first time in its existence, truly deserves some sympathy.

For most of us, the initial release of playoff rankings is typically an exercise akin to beating your head against a concrete wall. The fake seriousness, the inconsistent logic, the non-answers from the committee chair when you point out obvious flaws in their process? It's all such a silly little routine: Predictable and infuriating, even as we understand it's completely inconsequential at this stage of the season.

This year, though, we need to give these people a break and show a little compassion. Because have you looked at the playoff picture lately?

The 12-team playoff was designed to keep more teams in the mix and raise the stakes of late-season games as the calendar turns to November. It was not intended to be an advanced calculus problem, but here we are.

Given the number of championship-quality teams with two losses, the vast scheduling disparities that exist even between teams in the same conference, much less different leagues, and the quarterback injury factors at schools like UCLA and Ohio State, the picture is about as clear as a Jackson Pollock.

You can interpret what you see pretty much however you want.

Obviously, things will change quickly because this weekend is the most loaded slate of games in recent memory. By the time we're finished with Miami at Notre Dame, Georgia at Ole Miss, BYU at Utah, Kentucky at Tennessee, Alabama at LSU, Texas at Missouri and Iowa at Northwestern, much of the committee's future work will be done for it. By the end of season, if history is any precedent, there will only be a couple tough decisions.

Give these committee members some medals or something just for the effort because sorting out this mess is not a job for the weak.

Solving the puzzle is easy enough at the beginning. Unbeaten Miami is going to be No. 1 and Georgia will be No. 2, which hardly anyone could disagree with. Then we'll probably get Utah at No. 3 because, if this is like past years, the committee will care more about the Utes' 8-0 record rather than a schedule that was front-loaded with some of the weakest teams in the Big 12. Because Utah at least has one good win over Houston, that's not going to be very controversial either.

But once you get beyond that, it's a mosh pit.

Start with an 8-0 UCLA team that has one good win (at Oregon) but an offense that hasn't exactly looked smooth since quarterback Nico Iamaleava went down to a season-ending injury. How can you compare that résumé to, say, 6-2 Texas which has three excellent wins (Ohio State, at Tennessee, Ole Miss) but also two really bad losses to Oklahoma and Florida?

It's impossible because their seasons so far have almost nothing in common that provides a point of comparison. Sure, the committee's got all kinds of data tools and analytics that can help them sort through various components of a team's performance, but ultimately you have to either pick between record and schedule strength. That's not an easy call.

How can you compare 7-1 Notre Dame (beaten nobody of consequence, lost a great game at BYU that came down to one play) to 8-1 Indiana (beaten a slightly better set of teams but has needed a lot of luck to do so, and lost a great game to Ohio State that came down to one play)? That's a tough call.

On résumé, could you give Kentucky (wins over LSU and South Carolina, loss to Alabama) a slight edge over BYU (wins over Notre Dame and Arizona, crazy overtime loss to UCF)? That's a really tough call.

Despite being ranked No. 11 in the AP poll, can you even put 6-2 Ohio State in the bracket after watching the Buckeyes play such awful football at USC last weekend in its first game without quarterback Julian Sayin? Right now, without a timeline for his return due to an arm injury, you almost have to ignore everything Ohio State did for most of September and October.

What do you do with Wake Forest? No, the quality wins aren't there, but boy have they passed the eye test lately. And anyone who watched their 33-20 loss to Miami early in the season would have undoubtedly come away with the impression that the Demon Deacons can hang with the top teams in the country.

We've already mentioned 10 teams in this little exercise without even getting to the two-loss SEC teams like Alabama, Texas, Ole Miss, Tennessee and LSU, whose fan bases will be screaming bloody murder if they aren't in the top 12 Tuesday night because of the new nine-game Ess-Eee-See schedule that seems to be creating a totally new level of parity in the league.

It's a true "choose your own adventure" situation, with all roads leading to a bottle of Advil.

Poor Hunter Yurachek. Back home, the Arkansas athletic director has been on the hot seat so long thanks to the Razorbacks' football follies that his backside has turned a permanent shade of magenta. Now, even when he gets out of town for a long weekend of committee work, he goes right from the fryer to the frying pan.

This man's job is to go on national television and pretend like this process is ironclad, knowing quite well that no matter what ranking his committee spits out, there is no chance of being able to defend it coherently.

We play this game even in the easy years, and it always turns out the same: When someone asks why the committee picks Team A over Team B, Yurachek (or whoever happens to chair the committee) will give an answer using a particular data point or head-to-head result. Then he'll get asked why the committee picked Team X over Team Y and the same principle he just cited will go out the window and he's got to sit there and act like it all makes sense.

So in addition to getting yelled at by his own fans and media members for his regular job, he'll also get yelled at on social media by thousands of people who would otherwise have no idea who he is. Sounds like a blast.

It's enough to make you wonder why these otherwise busy athletic directors, who are under more pressure than ever on their own campuses, would sign up to be on this committee in the first place. Is the creamed spinach really that good?

Of course it's not. But it is a big ego trip with a lot of fun perks, and the job seems easy enough. Since the first year of the playoff, there have only been three real controversial decisions at the end: Ohio State over TCU and Baylor in 2014, Alabama over Florida State in 2023 and Miami over Notre Dame last year. And the only one of those three that truly seemed unjust was the FSU snub, which only happened because the Seminoles lost quarterback Jordan Travis to injury late in the season and were evaluated on a two-game sample with their backup.

So yes, it's a big time commitment for committee members to fly down to Texas and do these fake rankings for ESPN's benefit, but it's not exactly been a hard job.

Now the bill has come due, and they have real, thankless work to do. Hopefully the dessert bar will be worth the aggravation.

articles.title: Lionesses in Nations League draw: England draw France and Portugal
articles.summary: England have been drawn to face France, Austria and Portugal in next year's Women's Nations League.
articles.body:
England have been drawn to face France, Austria and Portugal in next year's Women's Nations League.

In Nyon, Switzerland, Sarina Wiegman's side were drawn alongside familiar opponents, having faced Portugal in the previous Nations League campaign, while France and Austria have both been recent rivals in major tournament qualifying campaigns.

The Lionesses will begin their campaign in Group A2 across three international windows in February-March, April and June 2027, with each team playing home and away fixtures.

"[France are] a world-class team," said Wiegman. "They have so much quality, they have power, they have technique and they have some players, of course, also playing in the WSL [Women's Super League] and at other top clubs.

"So it's exciting to play them because you will be challenged in the highest possible way and that's what makes us better.

"We played Portugal before the last Euros, when we tied with them away and at home we beat them.

"They're a team who can change their style from playing a possession game to being a little more direct, and they have some players that bring lots of quality on the pitch, but are also powerful in duels."

Now in its third edition, the Nations League also forms part of the qualification pathway for the 2028 Olympic Games and Euro 2029.

The four League A group winners will progress to the semi-finals in October 2027, before the final is played to decide the Nations League champions.

Scotland will face Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden, while the Republic of Ireland were drawn against Spain, Norway and Switzerland.

Wales will play Denmark, Italy and Iceland while Northern Ireland, in Group B3, will play Poland, Finland and Belarus.

Fixture dates and venues will be confirmed in due course.

articles.title: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold once again played poorly in brutal Week 8 loss
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks QB Sam Darnold once again played poorly in a brutal Week 8 loss to the Chicago Bears.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks were totally dismantled by the Chicago Bears on Monday Night Football , losing 34-17 in Week 8. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold once again played poorly. Darnold's performances are becoming a worrying trend.

Darnold completed 17-of-34 passing attempts for 188 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception. He had a second INT wiped out by a fortunate penalty. Darnold completed just 50% of his attempts and was held under 200 passing yards.

It's worth noting QB1 was also under constant duress. In Quenton Nelson's debut , the Seahawks definitely lost the battle of the trenches to the new-look Bears , who had Jeffery Simmons making his own debut. But Darnold played poorly independent of that.

Darnold averaged a season-low 5.5 yards per attempt. He had an identical 5.5 YPA outing two weeks ago versus the Denver Broncos . He's thrown at least one interception in six consecutive weeks, with a 1:1 TD:INT ratio (9 TDs, 9 INTs).

Darnold also isn't navigating pressure well. HIs pressure-to-sack rate was 21.4%, according to Pro Football Focus. It's 17.7% on the campaign. Last season, it was 15.0%.

When Drew Lock was the starting quarterback earlier this season, he outproduced Darnold in literally every metric. The Seahawks probably don't feel like they can bench Darnold, understandably so after they won Super Bowl LX last season. But Darnold is not playing well.

However, Fabian Hurzeler would mastermind the ultimate revenge three days later, coming away from the Etihad Stadium with a 0-1 win in the Premier League, moving to within just two points of City in second place, as Arsenal leapfrogged the Sky Blues into first.

As for Manchester City's record in the UEFA Champions League so far this season, the league phase has started relatively positively, defeating FC Porto 0-2 away from home, before narrowly losing out to Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad on matchday two.

A 2-4 defeat to the European champions would then be followed by a dominant 5-1 win over Greek giants AEK Athens - a game that featured a hat-trick for Phil Foden, as well as strikes from Rayan Cherki and Elliot Anderson.

articles.title: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel dies after collision with goalkeeper in Segunda Division match
articles.summary: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with the opposition goalkeeper during a Segunda Division match agai...
articles.body:
Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with the opposition goalkeeper during a Segunda Division match against FC Andorra on Monday.

The incident happened in the 97th minute, with the game level at 2-2. The match was abandoned after the incident. Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono was issued a red card for the challenge. At the time, the game was already down to 10 vs. 10, after each team had a player sent off in the last 10 minutes of regulation.

Owono ran way out of his penalty area towards the middle of the field to clear a long ball forward meant for De Miguel. He lept to meet the ball, colliding with De Miguel as his knee appeared to strike the Tenerife striker's upper chest. De Miguel crumpled into a heap and lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff arrived, with players from both teams visibly distressed.

De Miguel, 30, was stretchered off the field, with his condition described as "stable but serious" on Monday evening, but his health took a turn for the worse on Tuesday morning.

Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel is the individual who died after the collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono in a match on Monday, November 2.

His best season came in 2023/24 in the third tier of Spanish football, when he scored 16 goals in 35 league matches with CD Castellon. That helped earn his club promotion to the Segunda Division, the highest level of football he had played in his career.

He moved to Tenerife the following summer for a €100,000 fee, moving back down to the third tier for the 2025/26 season, but again earned promotion, scoring 11 goals in 29 games. He did not score in five appearances this season.

Who is the goalkeeper who collided with Jesus de Miguel?

Jesus Owono is the FC Andorra goalkeeper who collided with Jesus de Miguel, resulting in a red card late in the game against Tenerife.

Owono, 25, is an Alaves youth product, debuting for the club in 2021 and making 11 La Liga appearances over three top-flight seasons as backup. He was loaned to second-tier side FC Andorra in the 2025/26 season and made 20 league starts.

He was then sold permanently to FC Andorra this past offseason and, after a brief stint on the bench, regained his starting spot.

Owono is an Equatorial Guinea international, with 46 caps for his country. He debuted in 2019 as an 18-year-old.

Tributes for Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel

The club issued a statement of sadness in the wake of De Miguel's death.

"Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," a Tenerife club statement said.

"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can lessen this overwhelming sadness. We stand with his grieving family, with his loved ones, with all of Tenerife who mourn this cruel loss today."

Former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, who is a co-owner of FC Andorra, said in a statement, "I am sorry with all my soul. Rest in peace, Jesus."

De Miguel's former club Castellon said, "It's hard to find words when reality strikes in such an unfair way. We join with all our affection in the grief of his family and loved ones, whom we embrace in these terribly difficult moments and to whom we extend our most heartfelt condolences."

Javier Tebas, president of La Liga, said in a statement, "Today, we all share the terrible pain of an irreparable loss. My deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, team-mates and the whole club."

Premier League club Arsenal held a moment of silence during training to honor De Miguel's passing.

Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappe shared to his Instagram story a black and white photo of De Miguel with the added text, "Much sadness, there are no words."

Inter Miami and former Barcelona forward Lionel Messi shared the same photo to his Instagram story , with the added caption, "There are no words. My condolences and lots of strength to all his family and friends."

articles.title: Saliba back in training with Arsenal after being out injured since the World Cup
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — William Saliba has returned to full training at Arsenal, 3½ months after his last game — in the World Cup semifinals for France.Saliba has been...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — William Saliba has returned to full training at Arsenal, 3½ months after his last game — in the World Cup semifinals for France.

Saliba has been out of action with a back injury that didn't require surgery but an extended period of rehabilitation, Arsenal said in July.

The center back took part in a training session on Tuesday, a day before Arsenal's Champions League match at Slavia Prague.

Saliba hasn't played since being substituted out of France's 2-0 semifinal loss to Spain at the World Cup during the first half.

Saliba has struck up an impressive, yearslong center-back partnership with Gabriel Magalhaes that was key to Arsenal winning the Premier League title last season.

However, despite his ball-playing qualities and excellent reading of the game, Saliba might not be rushed back into the first team by manager Mikel Arteta.

That's because the man who has replaced Saliba for the start of this season — summer signing Ezri Konsa — has put in a slew of strong performances so far and Arteta might not be ready to break up the Konsa-Gabriel combination just yet.

One option could be to switch Konsa to right back, where he occasionally has played for former club Aston Villa and England. Arteta also has Jurrien Timber and Ben White as options at right back.

articles.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
articles.summary: Takeaways from OSU's first Pac-12 loss of the season
articles.body:
FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children's Stadium.

Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State.

Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching.

The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn't diminish what's being accomplished this season. They're simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now.

JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season.

Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State's tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter.

3. Self-inflicted errors can't happen in games like this

Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle's would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton's foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn't occur.

That doesn't even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits.

Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that's to be expected. Oregon State's offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU's rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it's not a particularly stout group.

5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field

Fresno State's 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there's one piece OSU's receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why.

OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule.

Tackling improved over the prior five games, but opponents' speed also dropped. Against legitimate athletic threats, the Beavers showed their tackling fundamentals, speed, strength and angles are still areas of weakness.

7. The areas for Braden Atkinson to develop are clear

Entz detailed Atkinson's reliance on his first read and susceptibility to being impacted by pass rush when it's not there. Of course, a defense has to have the talent and ability to do something about it. Atkinson's ceiling is high provided he develops in his reading of progressions, grows more comfortable checking into run plays and finds effective counters to the better defenses OSU faces.

Ojeda's three field goals should not get lost to the box score, particularly with a 54-yarder.

At 14-9, if OSU manages to make a stop and gain momentum, the game could have changed and the importance of Ojeda's kicks becomes paramount to the game.

As the sample size for OSU's kickoffs grows, so too does the success opponents continue to have. To allow a 44-yard kickoff return following a 14-play drive that spanned more than five minutes is inexcusable. OSU would literally have been better off kicking out of bounds, which has been enough of an issue as well.

The Beavers rank 114th in average kickoff return yards allowed and 126th on a per game basis.

Without belaboring a point that's been stated on nearly a weekly basis, the matchup disadvantage at No. 2 corner remains the Achilles' heel for the defense.

Against bigger receivers like Freeman it's simply a matter of when, not if, they will haul in big catches.
